name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,248

clue.text: Urgent request halved enjoyment

indicators.note: cutting something in half throws one of its two equal parts away, here the back half

blocks.note: pleasure is a synonym for enjoyment; only its front four letters survive

explanation.surface: Someone begging for something urgently finds their fun cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight-letter word for enjoyment is split down the middle and its first half kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal made to someone, often with some desperation behind it.

clue.text: Young man guards Irish landowner

indicators.note: a guard stands around whatever it protects, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a lad is a boy or youth
IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A youth acts as bodyguard to a wealthy Irish owner of estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish landowner' reads as one phrase, but Irish only supplies the abbreviation; the landowner is Scottish. LAD wraps around IR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a large rural estate, the local equivalent of a squire.

clue.text: Dire cameraman destroyed myth of Hollywood?

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, leaving its letters to be rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful film crew member wrecks one of the movie industry's cherished legends.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the film industry sells this ideal rather than literally owning it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal of rags-to-riches success through hard work is a national fantasy that Hollywood films have long promoted.

clue.text: I can’t remember main case collapsing

definitions.note: a phrase spoken by the answer, standing for the noun

indicators.note: a collapsing structure falls into disorder, so these letters lose their order and are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer whose key argument falls apart admits forgetting the details.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is something the answer would say about themselves rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering memory loss would truthfully say this phrase, so the words characterise that person.

clue.text: Attentive porter perhaps on resident’s case

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing of something, so only the outer letters are taken

blocks.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A hotel porter is attentive to the luggage of a guest staying there.
explanation.walkthrough: The porter is not a doorman but a beer, hence 'perhaps' marking an example; in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means watchful and paying close attention to what is happening.

clue.text: Restricts introduction of nuclear missiles

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: first letter
arrows are missiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: An arms treaty limits the deployment of atomic weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The missiles are ancient ones, not nuclear warheads.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow something is to limit or confine it, making its range smaller.

clue.text: Wears fashionable clothes belonging to guy? That’s fair

definitions.note: a phrase pointing at the quality of fair play, standing for a noun

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it up, so one piece is put around another

blocks.note: to sport an item is to wear it showily
the possessive of man, a guy
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: Someone dresses in trendy gear borrowed from a bloke, and another person approves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a plural noun but is a verb: the outer two pieces dress the middle one between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmanship is fair and generous conduct in competition, the very quality that 'fair play' describes.

clue.text: Legal case involving United’s sale

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: an action is a lawsuit
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football club such as Manchester United faces a lawsuit over its sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to whoever bids the most.

clue.text: High spirits and energy seen in a nobleman

definitions.text: High spirits and energy seen in a nobleman

blocks.note: liveliness and vigour, as in 'full of life'
a peer is a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A lively, energetic aristocrat full of zest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read as wordplay it is a word for vigour beside a word for a noble, and read whole it describes the answer. A life peer is a British peer whose title cannot be inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer holds a title of nobility, sitting in the House of Lords, but only for their own lifetime.

clue.text: Killer whale snatching men from Spanish island

indicators.note: to snatch something from a place is to grab it away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be removed
the Balearic island also spelt Minorca

explanation.surface: A killer whale grabs sailors off the coast of a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island must be given its Spanish spelling, which begins with the very letters to be taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the large black-and-white toothed whale commonly called the killer whale.

clue.text: Notice difference at sea

blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
a rift is a disagreement or split

explanation.surface: Spotting a disagreement while out on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb but is the noun, a printed announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean floating loose on the water, and figuratively confused or lost without direction.

clue.text: A great service

blocks.note: first meaning: a star performer, an expert
second meaning: a serve in tennis that the opponent cannot touch

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for good service in a restaurant; instead 'a great' is a noun for a star, and the service is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an outstanding expert in a field, and also an unreturnable tennis serve winning the point outright.

clue.text: Get flying boat home

indicators.note: something flying is tossed about in the air, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a seaplane back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying boat' is a real aircraft, a seaplane, which hides that 'flying' is acting on the boat's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or get hold of it.

clue.text: Ruling class setting up business?

definitions.note: a noun phrase read two ways; the question mark flags the second

blocks.note: first meaning: the powerful elite that controls a society
second meaning: the act of founding something, or a business itself

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the elite founding companies; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the dominant group holding power and the founding of an enterprise, or the shop or firm itself.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily from unending chaotic scene

indicators.note: with no ending, the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a total mess

explanation.surface: Someone staggers away from a scene of endless chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a chaotic scene is a plural-looking singular noun; dropping its last letter leaves the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to move with an awkward, shuffling, dragging gait.

clue.text: Learnt about new source of light

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone has found out about a new place to get light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is not the anagram signal here but supplies a letter; 'about' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp enclosed in a protective case, giving out illumination.

clue.text: Heard parasite’s spasmodic movement

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by the ear, so the word is spelt to match a sound

blocks.note: a tick is a bloodsucking parasite

explanation.surface: Someone notices a bloodsucker's jerky twitching.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary twitch, usually of facial muscles, that recurs habitually.

clue.text: Soldiers securing help for young woman

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: the ranks of an army are its men
aid means assistance

explanation.surface: Troops arrange assistance for a girl in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers as MEN is a standard shorthand, as in officers and men.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old-fashioned or poetic word for a girl or unmarried woman.

clue.text: Fanatic turned first-born son on mother

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards
one thing resting on another is added to it, so the earlier-named piece follows the later one here

blocks.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
in Genesis, the eldest son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A zealot's eldest boy rebels against his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The son is a biblical one; 'on' means the backward son rests on the mother, here written after her.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac is someone obsessively enthusiastic about something, much like a fanatic or zealot.

clue.text: Influential individual is feature of ski resort

blocks.note: first meaning: a powerful magnate or tycoon
second meaning: a bump of packed snow on a ski run

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a tycoon owning a resort, but the clue gives two unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a wealthy, powerful business magnate and a mound of hard snow on a ski slope.

clue.text: American sailor returned collection of charts

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A US seaman comes home with a book of maps.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the sailor is turned back; the American stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound book of maps, and charts are maps, especially nautical ones.

clue.text: Talented person murdered by brother, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the answer matches a spoken sound

blocks.note: in Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A gifted man is said to have been killed by his own sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talented person' looks like the definition, but 'person' belongs to the biblical victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilful or competent, having the talent to do something well.

clue.text: Protective cover breached before soldiers enter?

definitions.text: Protective cover breached before soldiers enter?

blocks.clueFragment: Protective cover breached before soldiers enter?
blocks.note: surface reading: a military fortification broken open ahead of an assault by troops
setter's reading: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg once its top is cracked off

explanation.surface: Defences are smashed so that an army can storm in.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, soldiers are thin fingers of buttered toast eaten with a boiled egg, so the breached cover is at the breakfast table.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin brittle casing around an egg protects it and must be cracked before toast can be dunked.

clue.text: Last part of school year popular with almost everybody

indicators.note: almost all of something stops just short of the whole, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a school year is divided into terms
in means fashionable or popular
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The end of the school year goes down well with nearly all pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last part of school year' reads as one phrase, but only 'Last' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal means final or at the end, as in a terminal stage or terminal decline.

clue.text: Model making a comeback divides opinion to some extent

indicators.note: only partly present, so the answer is a part of the run of letters that follows
coming back means going the opposite way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A fashion model returning to the catwalk splits critics' views somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says 'model' is a person; it is a verb, to sit for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To model is to pose, holding a position for an artist or photographer.
